The Trillion-Dollar Question Nobody Really Has a Good Answer To - Where Is the ROI?

We spend a lot of time debating how many GW of AI compute will come online. But the bigger question is: who ultimately pays for all of it, and can the economics justify trillions of dollars in investment?

I find it helpful to think about AI economics as a chain:

CapEx → Compute / Inference Revenue → Model / API Revenue → End Demand

One important nuance: the market often uses model company revenue (@OpenAI , @AnthropicAI , etc.) as a proxy for AI demand. But outside direct consumer subscriptions, much of that isn't necessarily ultimate end demand.

A company paying for Claude Code is still an intermediate customer in the economic chain. The real economic value comes when that company uses AI to generate incremental reve or reduce costs.

---
Let's put some numbers around 2027.

1. CapEx: US$2.5-3.0T

Assuming ~50GW of new global AI compute capacity, we're looking at roughly US$2.5-3.0T of total infra

Link
MSCI formally adopted rules excluding “non-operating companies” from its Global Investable Market Indexes. Prior simulations flagged Strategy (MSTR) and Metaplanet for likely removal, while SharpLink (SBET) was placed on a watchlist. The final affected list is due Nov. 11, with rules effective after the Nov. 30 close.
MSTR is a large leveraged BTC proxy for passive index funds, so forced selling could pressure the stock and weigh on broader crypto sentiment.

tweet.text:
MSCI Adopts New Index Exclusion Rules; Strategy and Metaplanet Face Potential Removal

MSCI has adopted new rules to exclude non-operating companies from its Global Investable Market Indexes. In an earlier simulation based on May 2026 data, MSCI identified Bitcoin treasury companies Strategy (MSTR) and Metaplanet (3350) as potential removals, while Ethereum treasury company SharpLink (SBET) would be placed on a watchlist. The final list of affected constituents will be published on November 11.

The new rules, effective after the November 30 close, will exclude companies that fail an operating-assets test and trigger at least four of five financial exclusion criteria. Existing constituents must fail the screening in both of their two most recent annual filing periods before removal. MSCI will also lift temporary index restrictions on companies previously identified as holding digital assets worth at least 50% of total assets, assessing them under the new methodology instead.
